title: Sam Smith Laughs About a Colorful Mix-Up in New Album Title 'Hazel Eyes'
summary:
Even famous singers make mistakes, and Sam Smith is laughing about theirs.

The Grammy Award-winning British singer and songwriter visited "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon" to talk about their fifth album, "Hazel Eyes," which came out in late August. Smith uses they/them pronouns.

The album was about three years in the making. Smith said the music traveled with them as they moved from London to their new home in New York. "It's about my relationship. It's about love," Smith said. This is also the first album Smith helped produce, working with Simon Aldred and David Odlum.

But there is a problem with the title. "I thought hazel eyes were brown, like hazelnut," Smith admitted. Hazel eyes are actually a mix of colors, including brown, green and gold or amber. The eyes the album was written about are an earthy brown.

Smith only noticed the mistake four months ago, after photos and plans for the album were already finished. "All my clothes were brown for the whole album campaign. It's a nightmare," Smith said with a laugh. "It should've been called Hazelnut Eyes. I'm changing the definition."

Smith said they wanted this album to feel relaxed, made with friends, real instruments and "singing from my heart and my soul."

Smith has won five Grammy Awards and holds two Guinness World Records. Their songs have been streamed 57 billion times, according to Billboard.

Instead of playing huge arenas, Smith is performing smaller shows as part of a world tour called the To Be Free residency, with stops in places such as San Francisco, Mexico and the United Kingdom. On the Fallon show, Smith performed the song "Oh Mother" with the TwoCity Chorus, a 28-member singing group.
why_it_matters: Even very successful artists make simple mistakes, and Smith shows how laughing about one can turn it into a fun story. It is also a reminder that words like color names can mean something different than we think.
